tagline.text: A two-tiered waterfall tumbling down stair-like rock north of Zamboanga

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Right after the rains through the early dry season (confirm locally)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~1,000 (per person, same-day round trip from the city)

children.text: Merloquet Falls is a two-tiered waterfall hidden in a valley in Barangay Sibulao, north of Zamboanga City. You have to walk down 370 concrete steps, but the stair-like rock face and shallow pool make the long trip from the city worthwhile.

Merloquet Falls lies in Barangay Sibulao in the Curuan area of northwestern Zamboanga City. Although it belongs to Zamboanga City, it sits close to the border with Zamboanga Sibugay province, so some maps and travel sites wrongly list it under Sibugay. It is about
2 hours
from the city center, so plan a separate day for it apart from your city sightseeing.
The falls come in two tiers. Figures vary from source to source, but the lower main fall is described as a stepped curtain of water about
high and
wide, while the upper fall is about
5 m
high. The two are roughly
apart, and a roped trail leads up to the upper one. Rather than a single plunging stream, the water flows over layered, step-like rock, and that is the falls' most distinctive feature.

The pool below the falls is shallow, and even the deeper parts are said to reach only below waist level. That makes it a place for wading and sitting on the rock steps to enjoy a natural hydro massage on your back rather than for swimming. The surroundings are fairly quiet and not heavily developed, which suits travelers who prefer a calm valley to a noisy resort atmosphere.
The trip is not an easy one, though. From the city bus terminal it takes about
2 hours
by bus and then about
30 minutes
by motorcycle taxi, and the last stretch of the access road is reported to be rough and partly unpaved. Once there, you must walk down
about 370 steps
, and you will climb them again on the way back. Plan it as a half-day to full-day outing that takes time and some stamina.

The lower fall spreads wide as water runs over layered, carved rock. Depending on the flow, the water may fan out in a thin sheet or split into several strands, so the falls look different each time you visit.

blocks.title: The upper fall and the rope trail

children.text: About
above the main fall is an upper fall about
5 m
high. Part of the climb uses a rope for support, so shoes with good grip are better than flip-flops.

blocks.title: Hydro massage on the rock steps

children.text: This is the activity that visitor accounts mention most often. Sit on the rock steps and let the cold water fall on your back and shoulders to relieve the fatigue of the long journey. Do not push it on days when the flow is strong.

The pool below the falls mixes shallow and slightly deeper areas, and even the deeper parts are said to come only to below the waist. There are plenty of rocks to rest on, which also make good photo spots.
From the jump-off point near the parking area to the falls, about
of trail has some 370 steps. The descent takes about
10–15 minutes
, and the walk through the steep green slope and increasingly dense forest is a sight in itself.
Travel write-ups describe the falls as a less crowded hidden gem. Except on weekends and holidays, you are likely to have a peaceful time in front of the falls.
A rental cottage is said to be available near the falls, at about

From central Zamboanga City, take a jeepney or tricycle to the Integrated Bus Terminal. The ride to the terminal has been reported at about
At the terminal, board a northbound bus bound for Dipolog, Pagadian or Ipil. Tell the conductor in advance that you are getting off at Vitali. The ride takes about
2 hours
Get off at Vitali and negotiate a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal). Agree on a round-trip price that includes waiting, then ride about
30 minutes
to the jump-off point.
Buy water and snacks at the store at the jump-off point and pay the entrance fee. Leave large bags behind and take only your camera, a change of clothes and a towel down the steps.
Walk down about 370 steps to reach the main fall. Wade in, enjoy the hydro massage and, if you have energy left, climb to the upper fall.
Climb back up to the jump-off point and ride the motorcycle taxi back to Vitali.
Catch a bus toward the city from Vitali. Check the last bus time locally, and try to be back before dark.

This sequence is an example stitched together from travel times reported in visitor accounts. Depending on traffic and bus departure times, you may often reach the city late in the afternoon, so start earlier if you plan to stay long at the falls.
Leave the city and follow the national highway north toward Vitali.
At Vitali, turn onto the Sibulao barangay road and continue about
14 km
further.
Park at the jump-off point. Older sources list parking at
for motorcycles and

Walk down the steps, rest at the falls and have lunch.
Climb back up and return to the city. Parts of the road are rough, so a vehicle with high ground clearance is safer.
Part of the road is reported to be unpaved. After rain the road may be in poor condition, so check local conditions before you leave.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Zamboanga International Airport (ZAM), taking about
2 hours
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check before booking.
From the airport to the city center, take a taxi or tricycle. Fares are negotiated or metered, so confirm before you ride.
To do the falls in one day you need to leave your city hotel early in the morning, so it is easier to spend a night in the city on arrival and visit the falls the next day.

At the terminal, take a northbound bus bound for Dipolog, Pagadian or Ipil. Some accounts also mention buses to Iligan or Cagayan de Oro. Tell the conductor in advance that you are getting off at Vitali.
Bus fares vary by report but fall roughly in a
range, and the ride takes about

From Vitali the motorcycle taxi ride takes about
30 minutes
. A 2020 post gave
round trip, while a May 2026 account paid
because of the distance and rough road. Agree on waiting and the round-trip price before you set off.
Some visitors say there are vans from the city to Vitali, but confirm the boarding point and fare locally.
From the city, follow the national highway north toward Vitali, then turn onto the Sibulao barangay road and drive about
14 km
to reach the jump-off point.
The last stretch is reported to be rough and partly unpaved, so a vehicle with high ground clearance is safer. If you hire a regular taxi, agree on the round-trip waiting fare first.

You can visit Merloquet Falls year-round, but the stair trail and the water volume depend heavily on the weather. Visitors report that on rainy days the current is stronger and the stairs more slippery. In the opposite case, when the water level is very low, the stepped look of the falls may be less impressive.

One write-up recommends August to September, after the rains, but that is a single source, so treat it as a rough guide only. Whatever the month, ask your local hotel or a motorcycle taxi driver about the weather and water volume the day before.

rows: Relatively cool, start of the dry season
Confirm locally that the flow is steady. A good time for the stair trek.
Go up and down the stairs in the morning to avoid the hot afternoon. The flow may be lower.
The current is strong and the path is slippery. Some say the flow is good right after rain, but safety comes first.

There is no lodging around the falls and most people visit as a day trip, so I recommend staying in Zamboanga City. The city has a wide range of hotels and guesthouses to fit your budget, and since you will leave at dawn, a place close to the terminal or the airport is convenient.

Visitors report a sari-sari store at the jump-off point selling water, snacks and drinks, but the selection may be limited. It is safer to bring a packed lunch from the city or grab something simple in Vitali. After the falls, return to the city and relax over dinner.
Start early in the morning. About
2 hours
by bus plus about
30 minutes
by motorcycle taxi means the trip takes a full day back to the city, and you need to be back before dark.
When you take a motorcycle taxi in Vitali, agree on the round-trip price and waiting first. One account mentions tipping the driver about
Leave large bags at the jump-off point and take only your camera, a change of clothes, a towel and water down the steps.
The stair path can be slippery with moss and damp, so wear non-slip shoes or sturdy sandals. One write-up gives the walk down as
10–15 minutes
The way down may be easy, but you must climb the same steps back up, so save water and energy.
Treat wading and the hydro massage as the main activity rather than swimming. Even if the pool is said to be shallow, it can change after rain.
When you board the bus, tell the conductor you are getting off at Vitali. Visitor accounts include cases of people riding past their stop.
Carry enough cash in small peso bills. Entrance, parking and transport are paid in cash on site.
On rainy days the current gets stronger and the roughly 370 steps become very slippery. If the weather is poor, postpone your visit.
Damp stretches of the stairs can be mossy, and the rocks on the way to the upper fall are slippery. Move one person at a time on the roped section.
The last stretch of the access road is rough and partly unpaved. On a motorcycle taxi, be prepared for the jolts and wear a helmet, and choose a vehicle with high ground clearance if driving.
Sunset comes early, so limit your time at the falls. After dark it may be hard to find a motorcycle taxi.
Travel advisories and checkpoints in the Zamboanga area can change with local conditions, so check the latest notices and local safety information before you leave.
Prices and opening times differ between sources and may change, so confirm them locally.
